specAnchors.text: understand the roles of oestrogen and progesterone in the menstrual cycle

primer.text: Twenty-eight days, two ovarian hormones, one repeating script. Oestrogen climbs first, thickening the uterine wall and peaking just before the egg's release; progesterone takes the second half, finishing the lining and then collapsing to start the period. This note maps both hormones onto the cycle's calendar.

modules.title: The Cycle's Calendar
modules.opening: The menstrual cycle starts at puberty and runs about 28 days: the lining builds toward ovulation around day 14, and if no fertilisation happens the endometrium sheds as menstruation before thickening again for the next round.
keyPoints: The average cycle lasts about 28 days, though it varies between individuals.
Ovulation occurs around day 14, releasing an egg that travels toward the uterus.
If no fertilisation happens, the uterine lining breaks down and sheds as menstruation.
Menstruation runs about 5 to 7 days and opens the next cycle.
Once menstruation ends, the lining rebuilds ahead of a possible implantation.

low.restatement: Build the lining, release the egg at day 14, and if nothing implants, shed the lining and restart.
low.analogy: Monthly redecorating of a spare room: prepare it, wait, then clear it out if no guest arrives.
low.examPointer: Quote day 14 for ovulation and 5 to 7 days for menstruation — the numbers anchor the marks.

medium.restatement: The calendar is hormone-written: the lining's rebuild after menstruation sets the stage, the mid-cycle egg release offers fertilisation its window, and the absence of pregnancy resets the whole sequence through shedding.
medium.analogy: A theatre that rebuilds the set each act for a star who may never arrive.
medium.examPointer: Name the endometrium as the uterine lining that breaks down — the term earns recognition.

modules.title: Oestrogen and Progesterone in Charge
sourceHeadings: Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
modules.opening: Oestrogen writes the first half of the cycle: it climbs from day 1, thickening the uterine wall and maturing the egg until its peak just before release. Progesterone writes the second half: low until ovulation, then rising to hold the lining, and its fall is the period's starting gun.
keyPoints: Oestrogen levels rise from day 1 and peak just before day 14.
Rising oestrogen thickens the uterine wall and matures the egg as day 14 approaches.
Progesterone stays low from day 1 to 14 and rises after ovulation has occurred.
Rising progesterone causes the uterine lining to thicken further.
A fall in progesterone causes the lining to break down as menstruation.

low.restatement: Oestrogen builds first and peaks mid-cycle; progesterone finishes the job and its drop starts the period.
low.analogy: Two decorators on shifts: the first prepares the room, the second finishes it, and their stopping time signals clearing day.
low.examPointer: Tie each hormone to its half of the cycle and to the lining's fate.

medium.restatement: The two hormones divide the calendar precisely: oestrogen's climb pairs lining growth with egg maturation so both peak together, and progesterone's post-ovulation rise sustains what oestrogen began until its collapse withdraws the lining's support.
medium.analogy: A relay where the baton passes at day 14 and the second runner's slowdown ends the race.
medium.examPointer: Quote the progesterone fall as the trigger for menstruation — that causal link scores.

glossary.definition: The roughly 28-day repeating cycle in which the uterine lining builds and sheds.
The release of an egg from an ovary, around day 14 of the cycle.
The ovarian hormone that rises to a peak just before day 14 and thickens the uterine wall.
The ovarian hormone that rises after ovulation and maintains the uterine lining.
